name: Coconut
description: A tall tropical palm producing coconuts, valued for food, oil, and fiber. Often called the 'Tree of Life.'
role: Coastal protection, food & materials for humans/wildlife, prevents erosion

name: Daisy
description: Small white-petaled flowering plant with a yellow center, symbolizing innocence and purity.
habitat: Open sunny areas with moist to well-drained soils
role: Pollinator support, ground cover preventing erosion

name: Oil Palm
description: A tropical palm cultivated for palm oil, a major global commodity used in food, cosmetics, and fuel.
role: Source of palm oil, carbon sink, habitat for some wildlife (though plantations reduce biodiversity)

name: Pinang
description: Slender palm tree producing areca nuts, chewed with betel leaves in many Asian cultures.
habitat: Moist, well-drained soils in lowland areas
role: Source of betel nut, shade tree, part of cultural practices, habitat for small fauna

name: Sunflower
description: Tall plant with large yellow flower heads that follow the sun (heliotropism). Seeds are rich in oil and nutrients.
habitat: Well-drained soils in sunny open areas
role: Pollinator attractor, food for birds/insects, soil health improvement (phytoremediation)

name: Turmeric
description: A spice and medicinal plant with rhizomes producing the yellow pigment curcumin, used in food and traditional medicine.
role: Medicinal and culinary use, soil enrichment, habitat for small insects

name: Torch Ginger
description: Ornamental tropical plant with tall stems and striking pink-red flowers, also used in Southeast Asian cuisine.
role: Ornamental plant, edible flower buds, supports pollinators (bees, birds)

name: Butterfly
description: Colorful winged insects known for metamorphosis (egg → caterpillar → pupa → adult). Symbols of biodiversity and beauty.
scientificName: Order Lepidoptera (many species, e.g., Danaus plexippus – Monarch)
habitat: Areas with flowering plants and host plants for caterpillars
role: Pollinators, food source for birds/reptiles, bioindicators of ecosystem health

name: Dragonfly
description: Fast-flying insects with large eyes and strong wings. Ancient lineage with fossils dating back 300 million years.
role: Predator of mosquitoes/insects, freshwater ecosystem health indicator

name: Leafhopper
description: Small, wedge-shaped insects that jump quickly from plant to plant, feeding on sap.
habitat: On leaves of grasses, shrubs, crops
role: Plant feeders (sap-suckers), prey for predators, sometimes crop pests

name: Moths
description: Mostly nocturnal relatives of butterflies, with diverse patterns and colors. Some mimic leaves or bark for camouflage.
habitat: Near host plants, light sources at night
role: Nocturnal pollinators, prey for bats and birds, indicators of ecosystem health

name: Weevil
description: Small beetles with long snouts. Many are agricultural pests, feeding on seeds, grains, and stored products.
role: Seed dispersers, decomposers, crop pests (some species destructive to stored food/crops)

name: Rhinoceros Beetle
description: Large beetles with horn-like structures on males. Known for their strength, capable of lifting many times their body weight.
habitat: Decaying wood, soil, coconut/oil palm plantations
role: Decomposers, soil aerators, some species are agricultural pests (damage palms)

name: Damselfly
description: Slender-bodied insects similar to dragonflies but fold their wings when resting.
role: Predator of mosquitoes and small insects, indicator of freshwater quality

name: Cicadas
description: Insects famous for their loud buzzing sounds made by males. Life cycles range from annual to 13–17 years.
role: Aerate soil (nymphs), recycle nutrients, food source for birds/mammals

name: Longhorn Beetle
description: Beetles with long antennae, often longer than their bodies. Many species have wood-boring larvae.
habitat: Dead/decaying wood, tree trunks, sometimes crops
role: Decomposers (wood breakdown), nutrient recyclers, some species are pests
